architecture.title: Fine-tuning on one Spark, and across two with FSDP
architecture.caption: Single Spark: lab 02 starts the playbook's NGC container with nohup; the recipes and the Hugging Face cache are mounted from the Spark's disk; the log goes to ~/w25/logs, which lab 03 parses. Two Sparks: Docker Swarm runs one PyTorch container per Spark, Accelerate starts one process per Spark (machine_rank 0 and 1), and FSDP gathers weight shards over the QSFP link with NCCL on every forward and backward pass.

nodes.label: ~/.cache/huggingface · ~/w25
nodes.sub: its own copy of recipes + configs

sequence.title: Labs 11-2 and 11-3 — start a job that outlives the lab, then read its log
sequence.caption: Lab 02 checks Docker, that no other course job holds the GPU, and that a Hugging Face login exists, then starts the container with nohup and returns within seconds. Training continues on the Spark. Lab 03, run any time later, tails the log and parses the trainer's per-step dicts into a loss curve and a verdict. In DRY mode lab 03 parses an EXAMPLE log so its parser is tested on every machine.

charts.title: Memory needed per recipe — one Spark holds 128 GB
charts.caption: From lab 01 (arithmetic, not a measurement): state at the method's bytes per parameter + a rough activation estimate for ≤300-token Alpaca samples (an assumption) + 10 GB headroom. Only 70B LoRA in bf16 needs two Sparks; with FSDP each holds about half the state.

charts.title: Bytes per parameter by method
labels: full, as the playbook runs it
charts.caption: Arithmetic: bf16 weight 2 + bf16 grad 2 + AdamW m and v in bf16 (2 + 2) = 8, as the PyTorch scripts run it (dtype bfloat16, adamw_torch). fp32 master weights and moments double it. LoRA and QLoRA add a small adapter (~0.3% of parameters at r=8) on top.

charts.title: FSDP traffic over the QSFP link per forward + backward pass
charts.caption: From lab 01, step 5 (arithmetic): FULL_SHARD gathers the other Spark's half of the weights in the forward pass and again in the backward pass; the 3B FSDP2 config gathers once and reduce-scatters gradients. Paid on every pass — gradient accumulation does not reduce it.
